correctness.rationale: The proof specifies all integer dimensions, positive parameters, Gaussian normalization and independent deterministic regularizer. Rotational invariance plus Sherman–Morrison give exact two-eigenvalue expectations. The unique unbiasedness candidate is forced algebraically; strict gamma-Stein/Cauchy–Schwarz shows this candidate has negative signal and positive null bias for every m>=2. Dominated convergence establishes the sharp opposite-order coefficients. Actual direct-matrix, quadrature and Monte Carlo checks total 893 PASS; these support but do not replace the quantified proof.

value.rationale: The determinant of Newton-step systematic bias is an algorithm-design question, not a routine matrix identity. The theorem exhibits a structural impossibility of exact finite-sample debiasing by a single deterministic scalar ridge parameter while quantifying residual signal and null errors with sharp, different orders. Hence averaging arbitrarily many independent workers cannot remove that fixed-m bias; non-scalar corrections are needed for exact unbiasedness. It does not allege failure of adaptive estimators or solvers.
